messages:
maggie: seeing a weird provisioning failure in eu-west3 — several GPU pods failing to bind because the local NVMe spiked to 100% iops during model prewarm. logs show 'attach held: disk iops exceeded threshold'.

maggie: i ran iostat on one host: 
```% iostat -xm 1 2
Device: rrqm/s wrqm/s r/s w/s rkB/s wkB/s avgrq-sz avgqu-sz await r_await w_await svctm %util
nvme0n1 0.00 0.00 1200.00 3000.00 2400.00 4800.00 2.00 35.12 1.20 0.40 1.80 0.25 100.00
```

maggie: this host has running prewarm jobs for the new image. suspecting prewarm concurrency + nightly janitor scrub + a SAN snapshot hitting the same nodes.

raj: ouch. any dmesg errors?

maggie: minimal dmesg, just blk_sched messages and a couple of read timeouts: `nvme nvme0: I/O 0 QID 1 timeout, resetting controller`. not full drive failure.

sam: is this correlated with GPU attach failures? i remember a recent rollout that increased prewarm replicas from 2 -> 6 for faster cold-starts.

maggie: yep, after we bumped prewarm concurrency attach failures went from ~0.2% -> 4% in eu-west3. when NVMe saturates, kube attach waits and backpressure triggers.

izzy: short term: can we throttle prewarm concurrency via the feature-flag or scale down the replica count per node? also reduce prewarm image parallelism to 1 per 15s.

maggie: will try scaling down to 2 replicas and set E2E_PREWARM_PARALLELISM=1. rolling it now.

ops-bot: deploy triggered by maggie:downscale-prewarm -> rollout started (canary 25%).

raj: medium term: think we need a node-local cache quota or cgroups blkio limits for prewarm worker to avoid starving janitor / system IO. maybe a per-node token-bucket for NVMe warmups.

sam: agree. also we should avoid warmups during the janitor scrub window (02:00-04:00 UTC in eu-west3). schedule prewarm to on-demand or off-peak.

izzy: another mitigation is to prewarm onto ephemeral:fs image (cpu stage) then warm KV cache separately so we don't hammer nvme with simultaneous model downloads and scrub.

maggie: question for capacity planning — if we keep prewarm concurrency low, startup latency increases and we might need more reserved GPU capacity to keep p95 under SLA. tradeoff: pay for reserved capacity vs risk attach failures. any cost estimates?

sam: rough calc: doubling reserved GPU nodes to avoid cold starts adds ~35% infra cost for eu-west3. but attach failure churn has hidden costs (retries, customer impact). recommend targeted reserved pool for hot models only.

raj: +1 for targeted reserved pools. also add observability: per-node nvme %util, prewarm concurrency, and a composite alert when %util>85% & gpu-attach-errors>1/min.

maggie: rollout finished, canary passed, all eu-west3 prewarm replicas scaled back. early signal: attach failures dropped to 0.6%.

izzy: follow-up action items: 1) implement per-node warmup rate limiter (SRE + infra). 2) add scheduler rule to avoid warmups during scrub window. 3) cost analysis for targeted reserved GPU pool (finance + product). 4) add alerting + dashboard.

sam: i'll own the reserved pool cost calc, will post numbers tomorrow.

raj: i'll prototype a token-bucket service for warmup requests (per-node) and link a k8s admission hook.

maggie: thanks. filing an incident note and linking this thread to the postmortem if we see recurrence. :thumbsup:
